corrected_proposal.title: ProPublica Reported GOP Committees Spent at Trump Properties; RNC Said Rates Were Market
corrected_proposal.description_short: ProPublica documented political committee spending at Trump properties; an RNC official said the properties charged market rates.
corrected_proposal.description_medium: ProPublica’s May 2018 analysis of Federal Election Commission filings reported at least $3.1 million in political committee spending at Trump Organization properties since the 2016 election. It listed at least $945,027 in Republican National Committee spending, mostly for fundraising and political-event venues. An anonymous RNC official said the properties charged market rates. The reporting supports the spending and conflict context, not the frozen claim that committees generally paid above-market rates.
corrected_proposal.description_long: On May 4, 2018, ProPublica reported that political committees had spent at least $3.1 million at Trump Organization properties since the 2016 presidential election, based on expenditure reports submitted to the Federal Election Commission. It said the vast majority of that spending came from Republican-connected committees. ProPublica listed at least $1,684,700 in post-election spending by Donald J. Trump for President and at least $945,027 by the Republican National Committee, mostly for fundraising and political-event venues. An anonymous RNC official told ProPublica that the properties charged the committee market rates. These records support a narrower account of political committees directing reported spending to properties owned by the president’s company while he held office. They do not support the frozen entry’s allegation that committees generally paid above-market prices or its claim of tens of millions in such payments. The market-rate statement is an attributed defense, not an independent price comparison. ProPublica also notes that its dataset covered electronic FEC filings and excluded some committees that filed on paper, so the figures are not a complete count of all political spending.
corrected_proposal.date_basis: The source reports spending since the 2016 election and was published May 4, 2018; this is the reported period, not a verified first transaction date.

source_fact_map.fact: ProPublica reported at least $3.1 million in political committee spending at Trump Organization properties since the 2016 election.

source_fact_map.source_excerpt: Since the 2016 presidential election, political committees have spent at least $3.1 million at various properties owned by The Trump Organization, including hotels, restaurants, golf courses and the famed Mar-a-Lago Club in Palm Beach, Florida. The vast majority of the spending — all but $731 of it — was done by committees connected to Republicans.

source_fact_map.fact: ProPublica listed at least $945,027 in RNC spending and attributed a market-rate statement to an anonymous RNC official.
source_fact_map.quote: An RNC official who requested anonymity to discuss the committee’s spending said that Trump properties were a draw for donors and that they charged the RNC market rates for using the space.
source_fact_map.source_excerpt: The Republican National Committee ranks second on the list for the current election cycle, spending at least $945,027, mostly to rent venues for fundraising and political events. An RNC official who requested anonymity to discuss the committee’s spending said that Trump properties were a draw for donors and that they charged the RNC market rates for using the space. The party uses other hotels for fundraising events, too: It has spent more than $1 million at Four Seasons properties in the past 15 months, for example.

source_fact_map.quote: The data comes from expenditure reports submitted to the Federal Election Commission by the committees.
source_fact_map.source_excerpt: In our FEC Itemizer database, we’ve started tracking details on which committees spend money at Trump-owned properties and how much they spend. The data comes from expenditure reports submitted to the Federal Election Commission by the committees.

impact_proposal.confidence_reason: ProPublica says its totals came from FEC expenditure reports; the RNC's explanation is attributed to an anonymous official and pricing is not independently compared.
impact_proposal.rationale: The cited reporting establishes political committees' reported spending at a president-owned business and a bounded conflict-of-interest concern. It does not establish direct harm to an affected population, above-market pricing, unlawful conduct, procedural abuse, or durable effects. The estimate therefore assigns no demonstrated harm, modest reach and institutional salience, and a limited self-dealing/conflict concern.
impact_proposal.basis: ProPublica reported at least $3.1 million in committee spending since the 2016 election and at least $945,027 by the RNC through its May 2018 report.
notes: Editorial comparative estimate, not measured harm or a legal finding.
